Oak Valley #1

In Stormy Weather

Chelsea Curto

3.85
47,741 ratings10,866 reviews
Rate this book
When lightning strikes, things are bound to get steamy . . .

Nothing can rain on Quincy Monroe’s parade. She’s a woman-in-STEM with a PhD in Atmospheric Sciences, the host of a successful online weather show, and has one million followers on her meteorology Instagram.

Quincy has spent endless hours forging her path in this male-dominated field, becoming one of the best in the industry. And with a new job opportunity, nothing can derail her success. Except for the ill-timed arrival of Sebastian Dunn.

Sebastian is her best friend’s brother, her long-suffering academic and professional rival, and a flashy TV weatherman from New York City that everyone swoons over. Everyone but Quincy.

Over a scorching Florida summer and record-breaking hurricane season, Sebastian and Quincy are forced into close proximity. Setting aside their grudges to chase storms and stay alive is one thing, but can they weather the inevitable collision of their hearts?

From bestselling indie author Chelsea Curto comes an academic rivals-to-lovers romance about storm-chasing meteorologists during hurricane season – perfect for fans of Ali Hazelwood and B.K. Borison.

September 5, 2026
Meteorologists in love? Well, don't get too excited. Let's just say I would've had a better time sticking to my favorite weather blogs than whatever the heck I got here.

I have a lot of words to describe In Stormy Weather, but if I had to pick just one, it would be excessive. Everything is just so over the top—the characters, the romance, the storm chasing, the working in a male dominated field, even the spicy scenes. At some point, you have to wonder if subtlety is indeed dead or if this book was just out on a personal mission to kill it.

Where to begin? Quincy is a meteorologist in a field where literally every single other person is a guy (at least according to this book). And every time she has an interaction with them, they immediately look down on her and disparage her because she's a woman. Now, I'm a girl in STEM, so I know what it's like to be a female working in a male dominated field. But how can there not be a single male ally out there for Quincy except the love interest?

And so we start into what can only be described as slavish ass kissing on the part of Sebastian for the entire 400 pages of this book. Every time they get together, he calls her amazing and brilliant and resilient and yada yada yada. Like, I get it, girl is accomplished. But no real person talks like this unless they're aiming to be sycophant of the year.

Speaking of compliments taken too far, we also have Quincy's two BFFs. Every time the three girls are together, they first have to take turns complimenting each other on how amazing and successful they are, before we can move on. Like come on! How do these poor souls ever find the time to exchange any useful information, when they need to preface every single exchange with many platitudes of greatness?

This book was primarily written in dialogue form. It must take up at least 95% of all prose in here. But just because something has the potential to be banter doesn't mean it succeeds. The majority was so bland and, quite frankly, an obvious attempt at filler that I often caught myself losing focus and skimming, just to get to something good. You add to that the never ending reassurances between the characters on how successful and awesome and badass they all are, and you can see how this starts to feel like a slog.

Back to meteorology for a second (the main reason this book caught my eye). It is a science of predictions, so everything comes with a rate of confidence. But the way this book tells it, it's all black and white, and the only two people in the entire world who can make the right call are Quincy and Sebastian. And they do so by taking a millisecond glance at the data, followed by Sebastian goading Quincy into being a "badass bitch" and telling their discoveries to the world. As if having your lover "believe in you" is the only thing you need to be good at your job.

And don't even get me started on the spicy scenes (long to the point of cringey), page length (also long), the incessant Truth or Dare (inserted into every conversation), Quincy's credentials (having millions of followers on social media, which was brought up again and again), and the storm chasing (putting oneself and one's partner and potential rescuers' lives in danger, just to "prove" oneself). Like, have mercy!

Obviously, this book does not believe in the concept of subtlety. It has the bones of a good romance, but it was firmly buried under a tsunami of "rah rah go Quincy you're a girl" messaging that got real old real quick. And if someone's really that educated and accomplished and they still have to put their lives in imminent danger over and over again just to make themselves believe it, then probably the right place to work through that is in therapy and not through their lover and their friends complimenting them to death.

So there you have it. I probably would've had more fun just reading weather blogs, which I will go do right now.

This was such an amazing story!! Women in STEM and men who are completely obsessed with them is a trope I'll never get tired of. The banter and the tension was top tier, I ate it up!!

Quincy is a meteorologist with a PhD and a host of a popular online show about the weather. Sebastian is her best friend's brother, a famous TV weatherman, her bitter academic rival who loves to rail her up and he's back from New York for the summer, chasing storms with her and being annoying.. The more time they spend together, finding themselves in dangerous situations, talking about their favourite topic and playing games, they might discover there is a lot more than animosity between them.. 

Quincy was such a force, incredibly smart, caring and so damn good at her job. I absolutely loved her show, I wish it was real, I would watch it religiously. The way others underestimated her, just for being a woman in a male-dominated field, made my blood boil. She was the best there is and seeing Sebastian standing up for her, always cheering her on and making sure she knew her worth was such a special thing to witness. I also adored her ramblings and the way her brain worked. 
Sebastian was witty, sweet, so caring, chaotic and always trying to be cheerful even when he's struggling, but ready to go to war for his Quinny baby. The way he was was there for her and the fact he was attracted to her intelligence, was unmatched. He listened, protected her and instead of stopping her from doing something dangerous, he just joined her. I wish we got more of him though. 

Their story was full of so much bickering, it made me giddy. The teasing, the Truth or Dare, the Ferris wheel and Reginald, the broadcasts, Claudia and the Waffle House, the ketchups, the tornado, the game night, the show, the beach, Georgianna, the notes, the picnic, the support, the passion with which they talked about the weather and how aligned they were with each other.. Their story was so good, I couldn't stop reading it. Not only did I read it in one breath, but I stayed up until late to finish it. I couldn't get enough of them.

This is how you write women in STEM, she was an inspiration. As someone who always loved thunderstorms, wanted to know more about natural disasters and was obsessed with the movie Twister, this was a deeply enjoyable experience for me. The atmosphere, the descriptions and them being in the eye of the storm, it was simply amazing. 

I can't wait to get more stories, I want to know everything about Mia, Harlow, Nate and Cooper. Their friend group, their dynamic and that found family feeling was the best!!
I highly recommend this!!

*Thank you to Netgalley and to Pan Macmillan for providing me with an ARC.*

— Rating: 3.75 ★ .ᐟ

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎Having already read and loved the D.C Stars series by Chelsea Curto had me going into this book with high expectations. As expected, it did not dissapoint. The romance aspect and writing choices in Stormy Weather were definitely questionable at points in the story, but other than that I loved it! The representation of women in STEM, the immersive atmosphere brought by the weather’s descriptions, the delve into meteorology. Chelsea is an author I know I can always go to if I need to be inspired by a FMC

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎Now, I was confused by half of the weather terms used in this book, yet it was so interesting! The plot overall had me really intrigued and was one of my favorite things about this story. With the illuminating descriptions, the weather phenomenons in action were illustrated really well and it was so entertaining to see the main characters chasing different storms. For me, this type of storyline is different from what I usually read, so I found it truly unique.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ My one issue with the plot is there wasn’t much rivalry happening? I mean, I didn’t mind personally, this book is just advertised as the main characters being rivals. There was only one scene where Sebastian and Quincy really competed against each other, the rest of said rivalry was only seen through brief recollections of the past from the characters. Other than that though, I was completely entranced by Stormy Weather’s storyline. It was exciting to see the different severities of each storm the main characters chased and how they were interpreted with different meanings.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎For the romance between Quincy and Sebastian, it was almost as good as the plot, but they were definitely missing something. They had such a cute dynamic and, albeit sometimes feeling inauthentic, they had tons of witty banter. I also have to appreciate the minimal amount of lust in this book. Based on the other books I’ve read from Chelsea, I was expecting loads of it, but the fact Sebastian was worshipping Quincy’s brain more than he did her body? I loved it.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎I think my problem was that Quincy and Sebastian hooked up a tad too early. The build up to their first kiss was anti-climatic and it took me a while until I could feel the chemistry between them. At times their dialogue felt too formal and therefore it was hard to feel an emotional connection between the two. However, when I had finally sensed the chemistry between the two in later chapters, it was immensely enthralling. I did individually enjoy both Quincy and Sebastian from the very beginning, so it was easier for me to get through chapters even when the romance was lacking.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎As engrossing as the characters were, some of the writing choices were iffy. I’m well aware of the inequalities between men and women, but I don’t think picturing women as better than men and making majority of the men misogynic in this story was a great execution of representation for women in STEM. It just felt overly forced, alike to some of the dialogue in this book. The moments when the main characters shared something emotional with each other felt like they were shoved into the writing at random. Sebastian and Quincy had very intriguing personalities, I just wish we had seen more authentic, detailed growth and complexity. Again, I did like the descriptive aspects in this book and it didn’t feel extremely repetitive, so the writing wasn’t the worst! There were moments I found amusing and, like always, Chelsea Curto had written the friendships in this book really well! (I’m desperate for Mia and Cooper’s book)

౨ৎ Quincy Monroe.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎I absolutely adored Quincy! Her rambling about weather was really cute and I loved that she ran her own show. Speaking of said show, it was so entertaining! It added a lot to her character and it’s connection to the plot was fascinating. Quincy was confident while realistically still having her insecurities about not being worthy enough to be in the STEM industry due to being a woman. For me personally, I don’t know much about meteorologists, but the elements incorporated into this story about her work were delved into a lot and it made this book ten times more enjoyable. She was kind to everyone who deserved it yet put those who didn’t in their place.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎This girl was the epitome of oblivious which did get annoying near the end of the story when it was blatantly obvious Sebastian was obsessed with her. I also wasn’t a fan of some of the decisions she made and her depth wasn’t extraordinarily written, but other than that I did enjoy her character! Quincy was so caring and the way she saw the beauty in destruction was inspiring. She was memorable in a motivational way and I loved seeing her get the chance to shine in a career she loves.

౨ৎ Sebastian Dunn.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎This man did not get the depth he deserved. Sebastian certainly entertained me from the first chapters, his dialogue was amusing and the dynamic he had with his friends was cute. I know, I’m using the word cute a lot, my apologies. Anyways, the thing is his character felt like it was based around Quincy. His emotional depth got more so glossed over and we didn’t learn as much as I would’ve liked outside of his relationship with her. Like I said earlier, I wish we had actually seen the growth in his character rather than it just being outright told that he was no longer ‘miserable.’

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎I still liked his character, I was obsessed with his dedication on getting Quincy’s attention and his interest in weather was just as enjoyable as hers. I loved Sebastian’s willingness to stand up for Quincy against misogyny while still recognizing she could do it herself. Also, the yearning this man did? Stormy Weather is one of the first book of Chelsea’s I’ve read where it didn’t feel like the MMC was full of lust for the entire book. He was just as kind and caring as Quincy, caring enough to save literal ducks during an intense hurricane. I love myself any outgoing MMC and Sebastian fulfilled that role wondrously.

⤿ read: may 16 - may 21 ; 2026

Review of advance copy received from Netgalley

Truth or dare, Quinny baby? 🌪️⛈️☔️❤️

Thank you so much to NetGalley, publisher Atria Books/Simon & Schuster, and author Chelsea Curto for an ARC of In Stormy Weather. Publication date is July 16, 2026 and you DO NOT want to miss this one! I already know I’ll be buying a final copy when it’s out so I can annotate and share all of my favorite quotes ♥️☔️

✨FIVE STARS ✨

I mentioned this in my pre-read, but once upon a time I wanted to be a meteorologist and storm chaser (before I realized just how much math was involved 😅), so this book immediately drew me in. Add a romcom on top of that? Say less. In Stormy Weather is PERFECT for readers who love enemies to (friends?) to lovers, banter that will make you laugh out loud, and moments that will make your heart melt.

Quincy Monroe is our FMC and I absolutely LOVED her. She’s powerful, intelligent, funny, and so caring to the people she loves. She’s passionate about challenging gender norms in STEM (and in careers in general), and she does not hesitate to call out misogyny when she sees it. Watching her stand her ground, advocate for herself, and still allow herself to be vulnerable was so empowering.

And speaking of calling out misogyny… enter MR. SEBASTIAN FREAKING DUNN. New book boyfriend alert!!! 🚨 Sebastian is witty, hilarious, deeply caring, and completely obsessed with Quincy in the best way. Seeing all of their moments together was *chefs kiss* especially their banter 😂🥰

Learning why Sebastian got into weather, seeing his passion, and watching how hard he fights for Quincy (especially against the patriarchy) made me love him even more. We love a man who listens, supports, and shows up 👏💞

This book is full of adventure in the most romcom way possible. You’ll learn about tornadoes, hurricanes, storm chasing, and meteorology, but also about love, fear, friendship, and what it means to truly be seen by someone. There are some spicy chapters, but they’re easy to skim and you won’t miss anything essential to the story.

I am desperately hoping this becomes a series because I NEED more time with the side characters… Harlow, Nate, Mia, Cooper… I’m not done with them yet.

If you love STEM romcoms with heart, humor, passion, anti misogynistic vibes, and tension, this one belongs on your TBR immediately ☔️♥️

It's insane how obsessed I am with this book ✨🥹🌪️⛈️!!!! The way every single man that Chelsea Curto creates is such a green flag ‼️ which obviously includes Sebastian Dunn. A love story between storm-chasing meteorologists who navigate hurricane season together... I'm sorry, but if that doesn't hook you to read it, I hope this does: “Whatever happens, I got you, Quinny baby. Okay?” 😭🫠 aghhhhhhhh, the nickname and taking care of you microtrope combo ummm please, someone sedate me 🫣

I loved the characters so much!!! ❤️‍🔥 They are both hella smart due to their knowledge of storm chasing, and you can see that in the writing, which I think impressed me a lot. Not only that but they used their knowledge and created a rivalry banter that was so fun to watch and see it slowly develop to something romantic INSTANT SWOON CENTRAL for me lol. The incorporation of the terminology to make it as accurate as possible, which Chelsea did such a good job, helps the reader definitely imagine the hurricane/storm scenes more strongly and vividly. Basically imo hurricane scenes 10/10.

Quincy Monroe who is a baddie with a PhD that hosts a successful online weather show, you can see as a reader the ways she wants to finally be taken seriously in a male-dominated field. I love her personality: ambitious, a risk taker, and veryyy outspoken. Yes, I am talking about her "I know what I want from you" attitude 😮‍💨🔥 SCREAMS.

Sebastian Dunn, what a man what a man 😩💖 He is obsessed with her from the start, and every time he said "Quinny baby," I melted a little 🫠 The way he was with her throughout their time together during hurricane season legit should raise all standards for men!!! YES, I AM TALKING ABOUT THE KETCHUP PACKETS 😭😭😭

For me, it was a 5 star read ⭐ not only for all I said before, but also because of how accurate and insane the hurricane scenes felt. I am from Puerto Rico 🇵🇷, and I lived through a childhood filled with mild to dangerous hurricanes. The way they both experience the season hit a little close to home ❤️ for me.

It is a career for some, but people forget mother nature can be cruel in the most beautiful way.

The chasing of storms and each other, as well as the banter, also solidified this read for me. I definitely recommend it if you love anything I said previously and, as always, want a happily ever after 💕

P.S. I CAN'T WAIT FOR THE EASTER EGGS TO BE FULFILLED. YES, I AM LOOKING AT 👀🚒🔥

╰┈➤ 3.5 stars!

chelsea curto, you have done it again!! 😩🩵 in stormy weather was nothing but a fun ride filled with soooo many things to learn.

౨ৎ quincy. a woman in steeeeeem!!!!! we love to see it. i truly admire a passionate, career-driven woman, and quincy is exactly that. she’s out here breaking barriers in a male-dominated field and doing it with intelligence, confidence, and so much heart. you can feel how much she loves what she does, and that kind of dedication is so attractive to read about. she’s not shrinking herself for anyone, not dulling her shine to make others comfortable, and that alone made me root for her from the very beginning.

౨ৎ sebastian. i’m telling y’all, this man is exactly where he wants to be :pppp the way he supports her is chef’s kiss. what i love most is that when he defends her, it’s not because he thinks she needs saving. he knows she can handle herself. he steps in because he wants to, because he cares, because he respects her. and that difference? it matters. it never feels like he’s overpowering her strength—he’s just standing beside her, fully aware of who she is and what she’s capable of.

and seb paying attention to the smallest things??? she mentioned once—once—that she puts ketchup on some of her food, and this man brought extra ketchup packets just in case she wanted or needed them. i’m unwell. that’s the kind of detail that gets me every time. it’s not grand gestures—it’s remembering the tiny, almost forgettable things and acting on them.

also, can we talk about the random weather facts sprinkled throughout the book??? i loved that so much. i did not expect to walk away learning more about hurricanes, but here we are. the hurricane chasing aspect sounds absolutely insane in real life, but in this story, it made everything so much more intense and interesting. the stakes felt real, and the educational bits never felt forced—they just added depth to the world quincy lives and breathes every day.

the banter? living for it. their dynamic feels natural, playful, and charged in all the right ways. it balances the intensity of the hurricane chasing with light, swoony moments that make you smile like an idiot.

i won’t lie—it took me way too long to finish this book. life got in the way, and i wasn’t reading it as fast as i normally would. but that doesn’t take away from how good it is. because once you’re in it, you’re in it. it’s smart, engaging, and genuinely informative. there are so many facts woven into the story that you actually learn something while being entertained.

overall, this book is such a solid read, especially if you love strong women, supportive men, and a story that gives you both romance and knowledge. i can’t wait for more people to read this because it deserves the hype 🌪️💛

Thank you to NetGalley, Atria Books, and the author for the ARC in exchange of my honest review.

i feel like chelsea curto did a fantastic job at capturing such intense situations which allowed me feel the panic, the anxiety, and the relief alongside these characters. when an author really knows how to immerse their readers, i will always praise them and appreciate their work!

✧˚ ༘ ⋆｡˚ quincy monroe ⋆｡°

in melanie’s words from love island, “i thrive to be as composed as you.” quincy commands so much power and knowledge—so reading about her just felt like i was watching history happen. she worked her ass off towards something she loves, and the passion she shows for meteorology is actually so inspiring.

July 6, 2026
‎❝ all's fair in weather and war, quinny baby. ❞


‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎first of all, thank you chelsea curto for successfully gaslighting an entire generation of women into romanticizing hurricane season. second of all, i would like to formally file a grievance with the universe because i am now expected to believe there are hot meteorologists out there trading elite, sexually charged banter while chasing category 5s like it’s a date night activity. meanwhile the closest i’ve gotten to meteorology is opening the weather app, seeing 96° with 85% humidity, which literally feels like satan's armpits, and immediately deciding to be a clueless shut-in because i refuse to entertain the thought of going outside.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ i. plot. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ in stormy weather follows quincy monroe, phd-wielding meteorology goddess with a wildly successful online weather show and big national weather service dreams. unfortunately, standing between her and professional peace is sebastian dunn, her best friend's brother, longtime academic and career rival, and annoyingly attractive tv meteorologist. thanks a lot.

when the two end up chasing storms together during florida's record-breaking hurricane season while competing for the same career opportunity, they're forced into close proximity, reluctant teamwork, and approximately seventeen thousand opportunities to flirt and banter instead of communicating like functioning adults. i, for one, support this poor decision-making. poor decisions have never looked so fine. or so wet. (the storms. i mean the storms.)


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ ii. the banter. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ the banter??? your honor, i would like to submit several highlighted pages, my entire kindle history, and my remaining dignity as evidence. quincy and sebastian spend half the book verbally sparring like it's foreplay and the other half pretending they're totally normal about each other, and IT WAS DELICIOUS. the unresolved sexual tension was so thick you could stir it with a rain gauge.

i was giggling. i was kicking my feet. i was looking up from my kindle every five minutes begging them to KISS. the dialogue was so quick and effortless that i lost entire hours of my life. every time i thought, "okay, one more chapter," chelsea curto would hit me with another exchange that had me smiling like an idiot.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ iii. quincy monroe. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ i adored quincy. women in stem who refuse to make themselves smaller will always have my whole feral heart. i loved how passionate she was about meteorology and science communication. you could genuinely feel how much she loved storms, forecasting, and protecting people through her work. it never felt like the career was simply there to move the romance along. it was part of who she was, literally baked into the fibers of her soul like humidity into georgia air.

i also appreciated how the book explored the reality of being a woman succeeding in a male-dominated field without letting that become her entire personality. she was ambitious, stubborn, funny, incredibly competent, and just messy enough to feel like a real one. a real one who would absolutely fight you in a parking lot over a radar reading and then look hot doing it.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ iv. sebastian dunn. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ i owe this man an apology because i judged him almost as hard as quincy did. and then he had the AUDACITY to be funny. and thoughtful. and patient. and absolutely, disgustingly gone for this woman. the yearning in this man deserved its own noaa grant.

i love when the male love interest quietly falls first while acting like he's perfectly normal about it, all while being approximately one mildly affectionate interaction away from combusting. sebastian, you are stronger than me because i would've folded for the baddie that is quincy monroe around chapter three, tops. i would've been out here naming hurricanes after her.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ v. romance. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ the chemistry absolutely carried the whole damn storm system. the rivals-to-lovers progression felt natural, the emotional payoff worked, and once these two stopped trying to professionally outdo each other every five minutes, they became such an easy couple to root for. i especially loved that neither of them had to give up their ambitions for the romance to work. zero "pick me or your dreams" nonsense.

give me two ambitious idiots who fall in love while tracking hurricanes over unnecessary third-act misunderstandings any day.


₊˚꒰ ⟡ ˙ vi. conclusion. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ overall, in stormy weather was charming, funny, romantic, ridiculously readable, and featured some of the best banter i've read this year. it somehow made storm chasing feel romantic, meteorology feel cool, and florida hurricane season sound more appealing than stepping outside my apartment in atlanta right now, because the heat + humidity combo is currently eating the state alive right now.

— 4.5 stars. ⋆˚☆˖°.ᐟ

big thank you again to Netgalley and Atria Books for the eArc!! this is not a book you want to miss when it comes out in July!! it is such a good book filled with a new favorite couple and high intensity situations🤩 the cover is gorgeous too!

Quincy and Sebastian are rivals to lovers, and he is her best friend’s brother. if you love those tropes then this is the book for you!! they are both in the meteorology field and have been rivals since they were in school, always trying to one up each other. when Seb comes back to Florida during some work burnout, the two reconnect as they end up chasing storms together, getting footage for her show as well as his docuseries.

their banter was incredible! i loved how they constantly nagged each other- at first to annoy each other but soon it turned into playful teasing. they were obsessed with each other, but he fell first and hard. 🤩 the readers will absolutely fall in love with this couple! they do have a spicy relationship, but you can skim those chapters and not miss the plot of the story.

i know nothing about meteorology and storms, but when things got super technical in terms and explanation, you’re still able to easily follow along!! if you like the twisters movies, this book feels really similar to this as they chase storms and put themselves in harms way for not only the thrill but also to help educate their audience on how these storms form/work and how people can stay safe during them!

highly, highly recommend if this at all sounds interesting to you!! i was super lucky to get this arc and hope to get a physical copy when it is released on July 16!! 💙🌪️

‧₊˚☔️ ‧₊𓏲🌪️ ๋ ࣪ ˖ ╰┈➤𝟓 𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒓𝒔 𝒇𝒐𝒓 "𝑰𝒏 𝑺𝒕𝒐𝒓𝒎𝒚 𝑾𝒆𝒂𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒓" ‧₊˚ 🌪️ ‧₊𓏲☔️ ๋࣭ ࣪ ˖

❝ I'm always going to love you. In hurricanes. In sunshine. In stormy weather. It doesn't matter. You and me? We're inevitably, sweetheart. ❞


The concept of this book is brilliant and the execution was even more impressive. Two Meteorologist that fall in love? Dare I say a perfect concept? But it was the execution of this concept that made me so obsessed with this book.

Our story follows Quincy Monroe, host of the popular social media show "The Rainy Day Show" and with a PhD in meteorology, and Sebastian Dunn, her best friend's brother and longtime academic rival. I love stories about women in STEM and the rivals that are obsessed with them. And when I say obsessed—I mean obsessed. Sebastian was so down bad for Quincy and I don't blame him one bit. She was everything. She was so smart and so feisty and beautiful. She's really everything that I aspire to be. Reading about her was a treat!

This was a dual perspective novel which is something I greatly appreciated. We got to see inside Quincy's genius brain and then we got to see inside Sebastian's, the one who been obsessed with it for years.

One great thing about his book is that it covers the academia side of meteorology and the insane storm chasing side of meteorology. I personally enjoyed the storm chasing side more because, truly, it was so invigorating to read about. The descriptions were so vivid, I was transported to Florida every time I opened this book.
This book was especially a treat for me because I live in Arizona, 🏜️ where it rains literally twice a year, so reading about this was definitely something new. It's not something I have ever experienced so a lot of the content of this book was really eye opening for me. My heart goes out to anyone who has experienced any sort of loss due to a natural disaster. I can't even imagine the devastation.
This honestly made me appreciate Quincy's mission to educate people on natural disasters all the more. Even though she is just a fictional character, she had an impact on me.

Almost everything about this book is perfection, I would just like to mention on nick-picky thing. Sebastian and Quincy were suppose to be these huge rivals but I just didn't really get that from their interactions in the beginning of the book. I wish we would have gotten some flashbacks to when they were in High School or College to really show that they were true rivals rather than relying on just telling us they were rivals.

Besides that, I honestly don't think I could have enjoyed this book more. The last 50 pages were wild! Everything came together so neatly and I was actually in tears in the epilogue. They were so sweet and I was so sad to finish the book and see them go. 🥹 I will definitely be purchasing this book when it comes out. I think that this is not a book you will want to miss and if you enjoyed her previous books you'll absolutely fall in love with Quincy and Sebastian. I certainly did.

*Thank you NetGalley and Atria Books for the ARC in exchange for an honest review. All thoughts are my own.*

3.5🌟 "I´m always going to love you - in hurricanes, in sunshine, in stormy weather."

I have... mixed feelings 🙃
This was my first storm-chasing-themed romance, and the part that spoke to me most was the weather depiction ⛈️ As someone who has always been fascinated by storms, it was so great to read this interest from someone else's perspective and see that there are actually many people who feel the same way 🌀⚡

However, the story overall fell a bit short for me, especially in the 2nd part of the book. I LOVED Quincy's and Sebastian's banter at the start, the flirtatious back and forth - the tension was so goooood 😮‍💨, but once they "got together", the story somehow became flat for me, and I started to miss a bit of the initial spark.
The end of the book, with them going off to chase an incredibly dangerous storm so Quincy can prove she belongs in the field, also left me feeling a bit sceptical, especially with them both focusing so much on safety and the dangers of the storm.

This was also the first book that I did 100% as an audiobook, and maybe that also had something to do with my perception of it. Sebastian's narration wasn't my favourite one - it made everything sound unnecessarily sultry: whether he is trying to flirt with Quincy or saving a woman from her car in a hurricane 🫥

on repeat 𝄞 ࿐♬ 𓍢ִ🎧ྀི ᯓ ‎♪ˎˊ˗
"ᴅᴇᴀᴛʜ ᴡɪꜱʜ ʟᴏᴠᴇ" x ʙᴇɴꜱᴏɴ ʙᴏᴏɴᴇ
0:08 ─♥────────── 3:43


If you’ve ever wanted a romance centered around storm chasing, meteorology, and two people who spend as much time arguing as they do making your heart melt… this is the book 👀 It follows two weather forecasters whose lives and careers keep colliding, creating the perfect setup for tension, chemistry, and so many unforgettable moments 🫶🏼⚡️

I have always had a soft spot for weather books, so my expectations for this one were ridiculously high… and somehow it still exceeded every single one of them. I genuinely think this is the best weather romance I’ve ever read. I flew through it because every time I told myself, “Okay, one more chapter,” somehow three more had already disappeared.

The banter??? Oh my goodness. 🤌🏼🤌🏼 Every conversation between Quincy and Sebastian had me grinning like an idiot. Their push-and-pull was absolutely everything I wanted, and I ate up every second of it. 🤭 Watching Quincy slowly realize that maybe she had Sebastian all wrong was one of my favorite parts of the entire book. Piece by piece, you get to see the man he really is, and he just kept surprising me in the best ways. Kind. Supportive. Patient. COMPLETELY gone for her.

And Sebastian… WHERE DO I EVEN BEGIN? The ketchup packets??? ARE YOU KIDDING ME??? 😭😭😭 That tiny little detail somehow became one of the sweetest things ever because it said everything about the way he cared for her. He was so unbelievably down bad, and I loved every second of it. The way he spoke about Quincy when she wasn’t even around, how proud he was of her, how he constantly believed in her… I was simply unwell 🤧

Quincy was also such an incredible heroine. I loved watching her thrive in a career that’s still so heavily male-dominated. She knew exactly how talented she was, refused to shrink herself for anyone, and wasn’t afraid to remind people she had earned her place. She was confident, resilient, and determined to serve her community no matter what stood in her way. It was impossible not to admire her.

This book gave me everything I wanted and then somehow gave me even more. It made me laugh, kick my feet, and completely lose track of time. I simply could not put it down, and by the time I reached the last page, I already wanted to experience it all over again. 😭😭 Without a doubt, this is an easy five ⭐️ read and one I’ll be recommending every single chance I get 😌 this is the first book I've read by this author and definitely not the last.

Also… Cooper and Mia?? I don’t know what’s happening there yet, but the trope potential is looking HOT, and I already need their story immediately 🙂‍↕️‼️

favorite quotes ↓

“I need you to know I believe in you enough for the both of us. I trust you with my life, and I won’t let you take the fall for this alone. We’ll do this together.”

“I wish, more than anything else, you could see yourself from my eyes. Because you know what you would find? The most beautiful, most deserving person worthy of everything she’s ever dreamed of. And if I could? I’d spend all my money, I’d barter with the devil, I’d find a way to give you everything you’ve ever wanted, just so you could see how incredible I think you are.”

“There’s her and there’s me, and someone with a whole lot of power decided I was lucky enough to live in the same timeline as her, and it’s the most overwhelming part of my entire existence.”

“I fell in love with weather because of her. I’m not surprised I fell in love with her too.”
